1. INTRODUCTION 
1.1.  Program name in Russian:

Сервис поиска случаев мошенничества по биометрии пользователей мобильного приложения 
банка на основе машинного обучения 
1.2.  Program name in English: 
Machine-Learning-Based Fraud Detection Service Using Biometric Data From Bank Mobile App  
1.3.  Program application domain:

The issue of fraudulent actions have never been as pressing as it is now in the banking sphere, with the 
spread of mobile banking and overall digitalization of the modern world. There are several different methods 
of detecting and disposal of fraudulent operations. One of the promising approaches to the problem of fraud 
detection nowadays is machine learning. However, not the whole spectrum of available data is now being used 
to deal with the issue. This project is aimed at creating a service which uses behavioral biometry data from a 
bank mobile app for scoring transactions in real time. The program that is to be created should provide a testing 
ground for the potential of such data and get the models ready for introduction into the bank’s security system.

3. PURPOSE FOR DEVELOPMENT 
3.1.  Functional purpose

The program is to be used for fraudulent action detection while committing a transaction in a bank’s 
mobile app, based on the biometric data of the current and previous sessions. As a result of the program’s 
work, a fraudulence score must be awarded to the transaction, given by a machine learning model. 
3.2.  Operational purpose 
The program is to be used by the bank’s data science specialists. Moreover, the program is to be adequately 
ready for the introduction into the bank’s fraud detection and security system.

purpose of operator’s work simplification, the least relevant configuration parameters may only be accessible 
directly in the configuration file.
4.1.3. Input data format requirements

The program’s input data are csv-format files, containing biometric data, collected through the use of 
the bank’s mobile app, as well as analogous tables in parquet and pickle formats. Additionally, some of input 
data is to be in the form of tables situated at the Oracle distributed data storage, configuration files in cfg or 
yaml format, machine learning models, saved in the form of pickle-format data, and text commands entered 
into the CLI. 
4.1.4. Output data requirements

The program’s output data may be in the form of any of the objects presented in section 4.1.3, which 
are to be saved during the program’s runtime, except for the CLI commands. Additionally, the program must 
be capable of displaying and saving graphs in the jpg format.  
4.2. Reliability requirements 
1) The program must correctly execute on any set of input data, and must not terminate with an error 
state. 
2) The program must periodically save its state or outputs for the purposes of continuation in the case 
of an error being encountered or the processing device crash. 
3) The program must terminate execution at a user’s command.

4.3.Operational conditions 
4.3.1. Operator qualification requirements 
1) The operator must be experienced in working with command line interfaces. 
2) The operator must be sufficiently informed on the operation of machine learning models, 
specifically for the problems of classifcation and anomaly detection. 
3) The operator must be familiar with the operation of SQL language, as well as Hadoop and Oracle 
distributed data storages. 
4.3.2.  Processing device hardware requirements 
Program execution is carried out on cloud servers with JupyterHub, Hadoop and Oracle. The server 
running the program must have at least 100 Gb of RAM and be capable of establishing connection with 
databases. The set of requirements for databases is under the NDA between the contractor and AO “ALFA-
BANK”. 
4.3.3. Software compatibility requirements 
For the program’s correct operation the following requirements to the device’s software must be satisfied: 
1) The device must have a Unix-like OS installed. 
2) Python 3.7 programming language and the latest version of pip package manager must be installed 
on the device. 
3) All the packages found in the requirements file must be installed on the device. 
4) The device must be capable of connection to Hadoop and Oracle distributed data storages.

6. TESTING METHODS 
6.1.Functional requirements testing 
6.1.1. Data reading from Hadoop distributed data storage 
The operator should specify the input data paths in the program’s config through the Configuration 
window or by modifying the config file and start execution of a model’s pipeline from the Train or Inference 
window. Raw features and target tables are loaded from the Hadoop storage. Their paths are saved in the 
config file, and the loaded data is then used in the model’s pipeline for either train or inference. 
6.1.2. Data reading from Oracle distributed data storage 
The operator should start execution of a model’s pipeline from the Train or Inference window. The data 
on user sessions will be loaded from the Oracle data storage. The path to the relevant table is saved in the 
config file. 
6.1.3. Data saving to Hadoop or Oracle distributed data storage 
The operator should specify the parameter out_scores_path in the program’s config through the Config 
window or by modifying the config file. Then the operator should start the inference pipeline from the 
Inference window. The calculated scores for target transactions will be saved on Hadoop data storage. 
6.1.4. Saving trained machine learning models 
The operator should specify the awad_models_path as outlined in section 6.1.3 and set the value for 
used_model to AWAD. Then the operator should start the training pipeline of the AWAD model from the 
Train window. The individual models, created and trained for every user in the dataset, are saved at the 
specified path. 
6.1.5. Loading trained machine learning models 
The operator should specify the awad_models_path as outlined in section 6.1.3 and set the value for 
used_model to AWAD. Then the operator should start the inference pipeline of the AWAD model from the 
Inference window. The individual models, created and trained for every user in the dataset, are loaded from 
the specified path. 
6.1.6. Feature computation for machine learning models 
The operator should change the used_model configuration parameter to SWC and then start the train 
pipeline. Features are calculated through aggregation from raw data and then used to train the model. 
6.1.7. Feature selection on the basis of relevance 
The operator should follow the steps described in section 6.1.4. For each user in the dataset, a set of the 
most relevant features will be selected. The selection is based on three statistical metrics of the features’ 
descriptive power. 
6.1.8. Assigning fraudulence scores to transactions 
The operator should start the Inference pipeline for either of the two models. After computation is 
complete, transactions are scored on the basis of fraud likelihood, and the scores are saved on Hadoop or 
Oracle storage. 
6.1.9. Applying configurations from a file 
The operator should start the program or move to any window from the one they are currently situated on. 
This leads to the configuration being loaded from the config file. 
6.1.10. Writing configurations to a file 
The operator should navigate to the Configuration window, and then set any parameter as described in 
section 6.2.3. The new configuration is written to the config file.

To start execution of a model’s pipeline, the operator should go to the Train or Inference window and type
